title: Swedish-Style Meatballs with Cream Gravy and Lingonberries
changes_from_base: All-beef mixture spiced with allspice, nutmeg and white pepper, with grated onion; rolled small and pan-fried in butter and oil, then served in a cream gravy made in the same pan, with lingonberry jam; no parmesan, garlic or tomato sauce.
summary: This follows the same method as our classic meatballs, but the all-beef mixture is spiced with allspice, nutmeg, white pepper and grated onion, pan-fried in butter and oil, then finished in a cream gravy made in the same pan and served with lingonberry jam, with no garlic, parmesan or tomato sauce.

ingredients.item: day-old white bread, crusts removed, torn into small pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
lingonberry jam (or cranberry sauce), to serve

steps.title: Make the panade
steps.text: Soak the torn bread in the milk for 5 minutes, then mash to a smooth paste. This gives the meatballs a moist crumb to hold onto once they're fried and spiced.

steps.title: Mix and shape
steps.text: Add the beef mince, grated onion with its juice, egg, allspice, nutmeg, white pepper and the meatball salt to the bread paste. Beat with your hand or a wooden spoon for 1-2 minutes, until sticky and slightly pale — this firmer mixing, rather than a light touch, is what gives these meatballs their fine, springy texture. With wet hands, roll into walnut-sized balls of about 25g each, making roughly 36 in total.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Heat the butter and oil in the large frying pan over medium heat until the butter foams. Fry the meatballs in two batches, shaking the pan to roll them, for 8-10 minutes per batch, until browned all over and a probe thermometer in the centre of one reads 71°C. Lift onto a paper-lined plate to drain while you make the gravy.

steps.title: Make the cream gravy
steps.text: Pour off all but about a tablespoon of fat from the pan, then add the butter and flour and stir over medium heat for 2 minutes until light golden. Whisk in the stock gradually, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pan, then stir in the cream and simmer for 3-4 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon; season with the gravy salt.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Return the meatballs to the gravy and warm through for 2 minutes. Scatter over the dill and serve with the lingonberry jam alongside — its sharp sweetness cuts through the richness of the gravy.

tips: Grate the onion finely and mix in its juice rather than draining it off; it keeps the meatballs moist and seasons them from the inside.
Shake the pan rather than turning each meatball with tongs — it rolls them gently so they brown all over without flattening.
Don't skip draining off the excess fat before making the gravy, or it will taste greasy instead of silky.
safety: Check 71°C in the centre with a probe thermometer; these meatballs are small, so they can look done on the outside before the middle is fully cooked.
storage: Keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen (without the cream gravy, which can split) for up to 2 months. Reheat gently on the stove, stirring, until piping hot throughout (74°C), adding a splash of stock if the gravy has thickened too much. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
